summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven compressed rotations, and preserve application write continuity with copytruncate. Configuration, functional rotation, scheduling, and reboot persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Forced an isolated rotation while holding the log file descriptor open; archived content was compressed and a subsequent write reached the live log.
Verified logrotate.timer is enabled and active.
Safely rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Verified the configuration, timer, archived data, and live-log writes after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed rule contains daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate parses it as a one-day interval with seven retained rotations before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A file descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote to the live app.log afterward, while prior content was preserved in app.log.1.gz.
logrotate.timer was enabled and active before and after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with changed boot ID 557d0837-6abe-4e52-9f0f-4e9a367cbc65. Post-restart checks proved the rule, active timer, compressed archive data, and live-log writing recovered.
